rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (just cause, relocation assistance, buyouts, retaliation)
rules.requirement: A landlord may end a covered tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause, stated in the notice. For no-fault terminations the landlord must pay or waive 2 months' rent as relocation assistance (3 months if the tenant is 62+ or disabled), give 30/60 days' notice, and offer re-rental if the unit is re-offered within 5 years. Buyouts are regulated and retaliation is prohibited.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance: 2 months' rent (3 months if senior/disabled) for no-fault terminations
citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause
rules.effective_date_note: Division as retitled/expanded by O-21647 N.S., adopted 2023-05-25, effective 2023-06-24; amended by O-21769 N.S. effective 2024-03-28. The Legal Aid fact sheet also gives June 24, 2023.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies longer than 30 days (not fixed terms of 3 months or less) in residential rental property in San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels, short-term rentals, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8), mobilehomes under MRL, nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities, dormitories, shared-facility rentals with live-in landlord, owner-occupied single-family residence, owner-occupied duplex, housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years, and separately alienable property owned by a non-corporate landlord who gave written notice.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief and damages including punitive; at least 3x actual economic damages for wrongful eviction; at least 3x unpaid relocation assistance; attorney's fees; non-compliant notices void; City enforcement.
rules.interaction: Consistent with Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 but provides greater relocation assistance; rights are in addition to state and federal rights.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable property owned by non-corporate landlord with notice
dormitories, care facilities, nonprofit transitional housing

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic software that analyzes nonpublic competitor data to set rents or occupancy levels, and vendors may not sell or license such software to landlords. Tenants can sue for injunctions, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
citation_aliases: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 11
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property
rules.effective_date_note: Official draft (D076) says effective on the thirtieth day after final passage with the date blank; June 2025 effective date taken from the Morgan Lewis alert (D002/D037).
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Software publishing reports from aggregated historical nonpublic data more than 90 days old or public information that does not recommend future rents; software used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.penalty: Injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation; prevailing tenant recovers costs and attorney's fees.
rules.review_note: Official text available is the draft ordinance with blank passage date; enactment confirmed by secondary law-firm alert.

unverifiable_exemptions: software used for affordable housing program rent/income limits

parsed.notes: Merged duplicates: just-cause (c64 official, c101 secondary fact sheet) and algorithmic (c65 draft ordinance, c79/c92 law-firm alert). D075 (link-only, source-of-income Division 8) suggests a San Diego screening_restrictions ordinance exists, but no provided document supports a verbatim span, so it was not added. No documents address local rent caps, deposits or screening fees.
